seo.title: Our Story — Why Travel With Us
seo.description: We live and travel these Balkan roads year-round. That is the difference between promising the authentic and actually delivering it.

hero.heading: We're here year-round. That's the difference.
hero.subheading: A letter from Almedin — born in Sarajevo, on these roads for fourteen years.

sections.heading: How it started
sections.body:
My name is Almedin Memović but friends gave me a nickname, Meme. I was born in Sarajevo in 1993 — in the second year of the Siege.

I came to tourism the way most good things happen — accidentally. During my university years I started working the front desk at a local hostel, and a lobby full of guests from everywhere turned out to be the perfect place for someone who has never been able to sit still.

The guiding grew from there. One of the leading agencies in the region took a chance on me as a young prospect. Three years later I opened Tallest Tourguide at 24 — cooking classes, alternative routes, experiences that felt personal rather than packaged. Then COVID came, and like so much else, it stopped. I spent the next four years building expertise in UX and design.

Now I am back as a Tour Guide, Trip Leader and a Product Designer
sections.imageCaption: Fitting in was always hard for me, standing out became a proffesional advantage when you are a tour guide.

sections.heading: History is personal here
sections.body:
What I had going for me was never a textbook — it was a lifetime of listening. My father remembers the Siege. My grandparents remember Yugoslavia. I grew up hearing these stories long before I knew what to do with them.

When I guide, I am not reading from a script. I am translating decades of family memory, shaped by fourteen years of work and learning from colleagues who built entire careers in this city. The result is a voice that carries weight — not performative, not packaged, just honest proximity to events that shaped a continent.

sections.heading: We don't arrive when a group books
sections.body:
We travel these routes in every season, not only when there is a departure to run. That is why we can tell you which mountain pass worth passing through, which family is making cheese this week, and whose uncle will share drops of his "maksuzija" rakija.

It is the difference between promising the authentic and actually delivering it.
sections.imageCaption: Standing out became a proffesional advantage when you are a tour guide.

sections.heading: A small team with skin in the game
sections.body:
Everyone who guides with us has a stake in how the trip goes. We are not a call centre booking a subcontractor — we are the people you will actually travel with, and the families who host you are people we have known for years.

Our friends are our colleagues and they supply everything that we cannot cover. Our tour guides, hosts, drivers have a quality guarantee.

pullQuotes.quote: Tallest Tourguide & Friends is back. This is not a return. It is a second chapter, built on everything the first one taught me.
We don't promise the authentic. We deliver it, because we live inside it.
pullQuotes.attribution: Well, it is kinda a promise

credentials.title: Born and raised in Sarajevo
credentials.body: Born in Bosnia, lived in Herzegovina, turned stones around the Balkan. The streets, the neighbourhoods, the people — home in the literal sense. That depth doesn't come from a guidebook.

credentials.title: Fourteen years in tourism
credentials.body: From a hostel front desk, to a leading regional agency, to running Tallest Tourguide from age 24. Every year added a layer no certification replaces.

credentials.title: Languages
credentials.body: English (fluent) · Bosnian / Croatian / Serbian (native) · Spanish (conversational). Local context is never lost in translation.

credentials.title: Genuinely small groups
credentials.body: A deliberate limit, not a marketing line. Small groups move differently — through crowds, through conversations, through moments a bus tour can't reach.

seo.title: Gostoprimstvo — The Balkan Art of Hospitality

hero.heading: gostoprimstvo
hero.subheading: The sacred relationship between host and guest — and the operating principle of everything we do.

sections.heading: What it means
sections.body:
When I was a kid I was looking my parents and grandparents how they prepare the house, meals, and rooms for the guests who are visiting. With an urgency like the ambassador is coming to our home and not a neighbour, friend, or even a random plumber.

As years passed I felt the same urgency and I as well as my parents started keeping the chocolate and sweets in least used drawer, far from my eyes so they can be brought in front of the announced or unannounced guest. I started identify myself with it, found a wife that has the same quality, and strengthen the relationships with the friends who are alike in this sense.

Realizing that Bosnian and Herzgovinian DNA must be filled with this code I looked for a warm human touch in form of conversation, smile, hospitality, sharing and all of those small detaisl which are what gostoprimstvo is.

sections.heading: Not a feature. The principle.
sections.body: This is a postulate of the life in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Everyone wants to feel as an ambassador because all of us are truly ambassador of ourselves, our family, village, city and country.

sections.heading: The coffee you can't refuse
sections.body:
The smell of roasted coffee filled the air. Specific moments: sitting at a family's table, the unspoken rules of the exchange, the coffee that is never just coffee.

Ritual that opens the door to everything else.

sections.heading: Why it can't be subcontracted
sections.body: Trust like this is built over years, not signed in a contract and faked. That is why a large operator can put it in a brochure but not at the table.

pullQuotes.quote: Balkan hospitality is not a product we sell. It's a practice we live and honor.

seo.title: Signature Experiences — Private, Expert-Led Balkan Journeys
seo.description: Not a tour. A private, expert-led journey designed around you — boutique stays, custom routes, an intimately small group.

hero.heading: Not a tour. A journey designed around you.
hero.subheading: Private, expert-led, and built one conversation at a time.

sections.body: Most of our guests meet us on a day tour. Some come back for something slower — a week built around one table, one question, one family history. These are our signature journeys: private, led by people who have spent their lives inside the subject, and kept small enough that nobody travels at the back of the group. We run only two of them a month, because they take time to do properly.

cta.label: Start a conversation
cta.note: These journeys begin with a conversation, not a booking form.

extra.scarcity: Intimately small departures · 2 signature journeys per month
forWho: You've done the big trips and you're after depth this time, not coverage.
You'd rather spend a whole evening at one family's table than an hour at three viewpoints.
You want an expert beside you for the whole journey, not an audio guide in your ear.
You're travelling with people you chose — a partner, family, close friends — and want the trip built around them.
notFor: You want to see five countries in six days.
You're mainly after nightlife and a checklist of landmarks.
A set departure date already fits your plans — our small-group tours will serve you better, at a fraction of the price.

journeys.title: The Balkans History Journey
journeys.blurb: A 7-day study-group-style journey with a resident historian, from Sarajevo to the southern monasteries.
journeys.route: Sarajevo → Višegrad → Mostar → Trebinje → the southern monasteries
journeys.rhythm: Two nights in every place, never one — history needs the second evening.
journeys.expertNote: The same historian is at your side from the first coffee to the last border — someone who has spent twenty years teaching this period, and lives inside it still.

journeys.title: Herzegovina & Montenegro Agrotourism Circuit
journeys.blurb: A private circuit through family estates and boutique stays, led by a food anthropologist.
journeys.route: Mostar → Blagaj → Trebinje → Virpazar → the Piva highlands
journeys.rhythm: Mornings on the road, long afternoons at the table — dinner is the itinerary.
journeys.expertNote: Led by a food anthropologist who grew up between these two kitchens and knows which family opens their cellar in which month.

journeys.title: Custom Family Heritage Trip
journeys.blurb: A bespoke route built around your family's roots, at whatever pace suits you.
journeys.rhythm: The pace is yours — some families want two villages in a week, others want one afternoon in one courtyard.
journeys.expertNote: We start with whatever you have — a surname, a town, a photograph — and do the archive work before you arrive.

process.detail: We listen first. What you've travelled before, what was missing, who is coming, and what you want this to feel like when it's over.
Within a week you have a first draft — the route, the stays, the expert who'll lead it, the pacing — with honest notes on what we'd leave out and why.
We shape it together until it's right — swap a town, slow a day down, add a table. Then we confirm the dates and run it ourselves.

sections.body: We are the team on the other end of the phone when your itinerary meets a Balkan road. Based in Sarajevo and working across nine countries year-round, we handle the ground — transfers, guides, hotels, tables, and the hundred small local judgements that decide whether a programme feels smooth or improvised. We are a destination management partner, not a reseller: your clients stay yours, your brand stays on the trip, and our name never has to appear on it.

seo.title: Where We Stay — Our Accommodation Philosophy
seo.description: No international chains. Family-owned homestays, agrotourism estates and locally owned boutique hotels — the kinds of places we use, and why.

hero.heading: Every place we stay tells you something about where you are.
hero.subheading: We work between two poles — agrotourism and homestays at the authentic end, and locally owned 3–4 star boutique hotels at the comfort end. No international chains. No generic rooms. We look for family-owned places with local character and hosts who add to the trip.

cta.label: Our signature experiences
cta.note: Private, expert-led journeys that lean toward the boutique end of this spectrum.

types.name: Homestays
types.body: A room in a family home, a shared table, and a host who treats you as a guest of the house rather than a customer. The closest thing to living somewhere instead of visiting it.

types.name: Agrotourism estates
types.body: Working farms and country estates with rooms of their own — home-grown food, quiet land, and mornings that begin with the place around you, not a buffet line.

types.name: Boutique hotels
types.body: Locally owned three- and four-star hotels with genuine character. Never an international chain; always run by people from the place — comfort without losing the sense of where you are.
